headline: Four weeks of near-identical volume confirms a stable consolidation phase, with yesterday's LT test anchoring genuine aerobic fitness at 4:24/km.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
Your 4-week load is essentially flat — 127 km versus 125 km the prior block, a 2% difference that's noise rather than signal. Average run length across both periods is consistent too, with nine runs in each. This isn't stagnation; it's a platform. The base is holding while you've continued to layer in quality and strength work, and that combination tends to produce delayed fitness gains rather than visible week-to-week gains in volume metrics.

The standout data point from the recent window is the June 27 effort: 15.73 km at 4:49/km with HR 161 — that's a meaningful pace-to-HR ratio, well within your demonstrated threshold ceiling of 4:24 @ 178 bpm, and it produced a load of 239, the heaviest single-run stimulus in this 8-run sample outside the 44 km June 8 long run. The two recovery runs either side of it (June 30 and July 2, both sub-140 HR at sub-6:00 pace) show appropriate modulation. The pattern of hard effort followed by genuine recovery days is functioning correctly.

The LT marker of 4:24/km at 178 bpm, recorded yesterday, is a concrete fitness anchor. Without 30-day baseline history to compare against, it can't yet be trended — but as a standalone data point, a threshold pace that close to your 10K PB effort pace (4:12/km) indicates strong top-end aerobic development. Watch how this figure moves over coming weeks as the baseline accumulates; it's likely to be one of the more informative single metrics in your profile.
watch_items: Track whether the June 27-style quality run produces a measurable LT shift over the next 2–3 test points — that session was heavy enough to drive adaptation.
Monitor how HR responds on easy runs post-LT test; a slight HR elevation for 48–72 hours would be normal, and would confirm the test was genuinely taxing.
